text: Why must a radio signal be modulated onto a carrier rather than transmitted at baseband?
choices: Baseband signals are illegal in most jurisdictions
An efficient antenna is a substantial fraction of a wavelength, and baseband wavelengths are kilometres long
explanation: A 3 kHz baseband signal has a 100 km wavelength, so a quarter-wave antenna would be 25 km tall. Moving it to 900 MHz gives a 33 cm wavelength and an 8.3 cm antenna. The second, independent reason is that modulation permits frequency-division multiplexing.
